beats.notes: Equal quarter-note kicks only. This shared foundation is not itself a complete genre.
beats.title: Four to the floor / bare pulse

beats.notes: Original swung variant: extra ghost kicks and claps; not a transcription of a named track.
beats.title: Jackin house / ghost-kick turnaround

beats.notes: A deliberately broken alternative; not all techno uses a quarter-note kick.
beats.title: Techno / broken kick study

beats.notes: Original three-sixteenth percussion cycle over 4/4: both layers close after three bars.
beats.title: Techno / three-step percussion cycle

beats.notes: Backbeats on 2/4; the second kick sits on the & of 3. Off-grid hats supply shuffle.
beats.title: UK garage / two-step foundation

beats.notes: Garage also has a four-to-the-floor branch; it is not all two-step.
beats.title: UK garage / four-four shuffle

beats.notes: Bass onsets are included as movement cues. Audio uses a simple synth, not a sampled Reese patch.
beats.title: Speed garage / offbeat bass answers

beats.notes: A 140 BPM syncopated study; grime has no single mandatory snare pattern.
beats.title: Grime / displaced snare conversation

beats.notes: 3+3+2 sixteenth grouping is not a tuplet: the grid here remains straight.
beats.title: UK drill / grouped hats

beats.notes: Snare: beat 3 in bar one, beat 4 in bar two. This is one common design, not a rule for all drill.
beats.title: UK drill / moving second-bar snare

beats.notes: The added hat fill uses rational tuplets; grouped hats and triplet rolls remain distinct concepts.
beats.title: UK drill / true triplet hat fill

beats.notes: Gregory C. Coleman / The Winstons, Amen, Brother. Four bars, not a generic 2-bar loop. Timing/velocity are approximations; no original recording or measured human microtiming.
beats.title: Amen / four-bar structural study

beats.notes: A/B study: only quiet snares removed. This deliberately simplified version is not the complete Amen.
beats.title: Amen / remove the ghost snares

beats.notes: Original chopped-break-style arrangement, not the original Amen sequence.
beats.title: Jungle / rearranged break fragments

beats.notes: Four-bar original phrase: the final half uses fewer main snares, not a tempo change.
beats.title: Jungle / full-time to half-time answer

beats.notes: Offbeat bass/pulse is included. A rhythmic sketch cannot supply trance harmony, timbre or arrangement.
beats.title: Trance / offbeat lift

beats.notes: Quarter-note kick version with offbeat snare answers; one useful dembow foundation, not every dancehall rhythm.
beats.title: Reggaeton / dembow answer

beats.notes: An original percussion and log-drum-style bass rhythm. Pitched bass is a cue lane, not a downloaded sample.
beats.title: Amapiano / shaker and bass-percussion study

beats.notes: Kick on zero-based sixteenths 0,4,8,11,14: two quarters then 3+3+2 sixteenths. Not triplets. Accompaniment is authored.
beats.title: Jersey / five-kick foundation

beats.notes: Same signature kick cycle, original two-bar response and quiet snare pickup; not a new canonical kick pattern.
beats.title: Jersey / call and turnaround

beats.notes: Authored sparse drum/bass conversation. Bass replies include genuine thirds of a beat; not a genre-wide transcription.
beats.title: Footwork / triplet bass reply

beats.notes: An original interrupted 808-style study; the suggested tempo is an audition setting, not a classification rule.
beats.title: Footwork / interrupted half-time

beats.notes: Tom/rim motion is an original response to Roska’s discussion of skippy, travelling percussion, not one of his tracks.
beats.title: UK funky / tom-led skips

beats.notes: Kick gaps and percussion answers produce a different phrase without applying swing to the main anchors.
beats.title: UK funky / broken response

beats.notes: Original broken-beat study: the first-bar closing snare is displaced by half a beat. Not a universal broken-beat grid.
beats.title: Broken beat / early-and-late answers

beats.notes: Only selected upper-percussion off-sixteenths swing; bass and main drums keep their authored positions.
beats.title: Broken beat / shuffled rim circuit

beats.notes: Four-floor foundation with an original interlocking bell/tom arrangement. Rim synthesises a bell-like timing cue only.
beats.title: Afro house / bell and kick weave

beats.notes: Three equal tom accents per four-beat bar are retained as exact fractions over the quarter-kick layer.
beats.title: Afro house / three-over-four percussion

beats.notes: Original sparse broken-kick design informed by DJ Lag’s description; no named Gqom track is transcribed.
beats.title: Gqom / broken-kick space study

beats.notes: A second authored conversation between low drums. Synthetic toms are timing cues, not authentic sample reconstruction.
beats.title: Gqom / staggered drum exchange

beats.notes: Original low-drum/syncopation study, not a definitive tamborzão transcription. Distinct from drift phonk.
beats.title: Baile funk / low-drum conversation

beats.notes: Original programmed variation using contrasting low/percussive answers; not a recording or scene-complete model.
beats.title: Baile funk / syncopated answer

beats.notes: Kick and cross-stick coincide on beat 3 with beat 1 left empty in those lanes; bass is an original accompaniment.
beats.title: Reggae / one-drop foundation

beats.notes: Quarter-note kick with beat-3 cross-stick; the same four-floor kick has a different surrounding rhythmic context.
beats.title: Dub / steppers foundation

beats.notes: Illustrative rockers-style kick on 1 and 3; variants exist. Not every rockers groove uses this exact grid.
beats.title: Reggae / kick-on-one-and-three study

beats.notes: Two-bar 3-2 son clave: 1, & of 2, 4 | 2, 3. Club kick/shaker orchestration is original.
beats.title: Latin club / 3-2 son clave

beats.notes: Two-bar 2-3 son clave reverses the two sides. Not interchangeable against an unchanged melodic phrase.
beats.title: Latin club / 2-3 son clave

beats.notes: Original kick-bass-bass-bass sixteenth arrangement: three straight subdivisions, not a triplet. Short synth cues stand in for bass articulation.
beats.title: Psy / straight rolling bass gaps

beats.notes: Quarter kicks alternate with offbeat eighth-note bass; supporting hats and claps are authored.
beats.title: Trance / offbeat bass exchange

beats.notes: Late-beat bass onsets cue a swelling response. Audio is simple bass synthesis, not a complete reverse-bass sound-design recreation.
beats.title: Hard dance / delayed bass swell cues

beats.notes: Original machine-style arrangement: straight kick/backbeat beneath a busy rim part and subtly shuffled hats.
beats.title: Italo / machine rim conversation

beats.notes: Original broken electro study using a drum-machine backbeat and syncopated kick/bass; no sampled break.
beats.title: Electro / asymmetric machine break

beats.notes: Original house grid with an asymmetric bass rhythm. This is not a 303 timbre emulator; acid character cannot be encoded by rhythm alone.
beats.title: Acid house / syncopated machine accents

beats.notes: Explicit delayed low-end cues approximate a kick-tail conversation, not acoustic convolution or a canonical techno beat.
beats.title: Techno / delayed low-end answer

beats.notes: An original rim-led two-step variant; selected upper-percussion subdivisions use 5:3 swing.
beats.title: Garage / rim-led skipping pocket

beats.notes: Original rolling break with a late first-bar pickup and quieter internal snares; not another recorded break transcription.
beats.title: DnB / kick pickup and ghost reply

beats.notes: Original break rearrangement with changing second-bar snare placement. Amen 05 remains unchanged as a separate study.
beats.title: Jungle / two-bar switchback

beats.notes: An original low-end/percussion call-and-response. Synth bass marks log-drum events but is not an authentic log-drum instrument model.
beats.title: Amapiano / log-like bass answer

beats.notes: An original sparse dancehall-influenced arrangement with displaced rim replies; not a historical riddim transcription.
beats.title: Dancehall / spacious offbeat replies

beats.notes: Common dembow-style snare displacement under quarter kicks with an original second-bar pickup and bass phrase.
beats.title: Reggaeton / dembow with pickup answer
